prediction: Ignition is triggered by a single winning representation crossing threshold; the theory quantifies stimulus strength and attention, not the cardinality of the competing set. No published GNWT prediction indexes access to how many policies compete.
Competition for the workspace is assumed but its degree is not a predictor variable; predictions are stated over visibility/threshold, not over conflict magnitude.
Broadcast is content-neutral by construction: any representation that wins gains global availability. Valence can be a workspace content but is not predicted to shift access thresholds.
The workspace is defined over cortical (fronto-parietal) processors; autonomic effectors are not among the consumer systems whose recruitment is predicted.
"Global availability" is organism-wide in spirit, but the operationalisation is cortical ignition and P3b; no joint cortical-autonomic metric is specified.
No prediction about the dimensionality of experienced content; the theory predicts presence/absence of access.
Metacognition is argued to be a needed addition to the workspace rather than a quantity the theory itself predicts.
Late (~250-400 ms) non-linear ignition of a fronto-parietal network, P3b, sustained prefrontal activity; tested and partly falsified at stimulus offset by the adversarial collaboration.
phi is computed on the cause-effect structure of a substrate in a state; the number of competing action policies is not a term in the formalism.
Exclusion/integration postulates concern partitions of the substrate, not incompatibility of behavioural options.

IIT 4.0 explicitly lists affect among candidate properties of experience that are NOT essential — experiences lacking it are held to be conceivable and achievable; valence is therefore excluded from the axioms.
Substrate is defined by intrinsic cause-effect power; visceral channels have no privileged status.
No organism-wide coherence prediction; the main complex may be a cortical subset.
The quality of experience is identified with the structure of distinctions and relations unfolded from the substrate — a formal claim about the geometry, hence dimensionality, of phenomenal space.
Metacognitive accuracy is not a theoretical quantity; report is not required for phi.
Sustained posterior synchronisation within a posterior "hot zone" for the duration of the percept; tested and challenged by the adversarial collaboration.
Phenomenality is fixed by local recurrent interaction in sensory cortex; no term for competing policies.
No prediction over conflict magnitude.
Recurrence is specified over feedforward/feedback sensory sweeps, indifferent to content valence.
Theory is formulated for sensory (chiefly visual) cortex.
Explicitly denies that global availability is required for phenomenality.
No dimensionality claim.
Report and metacognition are downstream of phenomenality by design.
Local recurrent processing in sensory areas, ~100-200 ms; dissociable from the late global signature.
Higher-order state space is defined over perceptual generative models, not over action policies.
No conflict-magnitude term.
Higher-order theory has been extended to emotional consciousness, but the extension asserts a common higher-order mechanism rather than predicting differential access thresholds for valenced content.
LeDoux and Brown route bodily/survival-circuit signals into higher-order representation, without quantitative predictions on autonomic recruitment.
Awareness is local and prefrontal; no organism-wide coherence claim.
HOSS makes the sharp claim that the awareness state is low-dimensional — a 1D continuum from absent to present — nested asymmetrically above a high-dimensional perceptual space.
Core measurable: metacognitive sensitivity/efficiency (meta-d prime), calibration of confidence, and its dissociation from first-order performance.
Prefrontal involvement in awareness reports; global ignition reproduced as a consequence of asymmetric state-space inference.
Awareness is a schematic model of attention; competing policies are not represented.
No conflict term.
The attention schema models attentional state, not valence.
Formulated over attentional and body schemas, not visceral regulation.
No organism-wide coherence prediction.
The schema is explicitly simplified and non-physical, implying low dimensionality, but no dimensionality is measured or predicted.
Predicts systematic inaccuracy of the schema; accuracy of introspection is a consequence rather than a quantified predictor.
Temporo-parietal junction and superior temporal sulcus as substrate of the attention schema; causal manipulations predicted to disrupt awareness.
Precision-weighted prediction error is the currency; policy cardinality is not a predictor of access.
Policy selection appears as active inference over competing policies, but the consciousness-relevant predictions are about inference, not about how many policies compete.
Valence is derived: emotion is interoceptive inference, and valence has been formally linked to the rate of change of free energy.
Central and distinctive: interoceptive and autonomic channels are the substrate of emotion and embodied selfhood, with allostatic regulation as the control objective.
Allostasis is organism-wide and a large-scale interoceptive-allostatic system has been identified, but no joint cortical-autonomic metric is proposed as a criterion of conscious access.
Experience as compressed inference implies dimensionality reduction; no quantitative prediction of phenomenal dimensionality.
Precision (inverse variance) is the theory's own control parameter, and interoceptive accuracy is dissociated from interoceptive awareness/sensibility.
Offers a systematic basis for identifying neural correlates but does not commit to a single cortical access signature.

PRISM: phenomenal states are required when multiple supramodular systems send simultaneous, competing inclinations to the skeletomotor output system — the number of concurrent inclinations is the theory's own trigger variable.
Directly measured: merely sustaining incompatible skeletomotor intentions in a motionless state produces stronger subjective effects than compatible intentions.
Conscious conflict is described as having affective consequences and is linked to failures of self-control, but valence of content is not itself a predictor of access.
A sharp, testable negative: conflict in a smooth-muscle effector (pupillary light reflex) produces no comparable change in conscious experience; phenomenal states serve skeletomotor integration only.
Phenomenal states integrate systems competing for skeletal muscle; no organism-wide coherence measure including autonomic channels is proposed.
No dimensionality prediction.
Integration is stated as co-presence of contents; metarepresentational precision plays no role.

Subjective conflict from sustained incompatible intentions was associated with left postcentral (somatosensory) cortex; a candidate substrate is named, but no discriminating cortical access signature is staked.

The function of the conscious field is still stated as integration of multiple skeletomotor inclinations, but the passive-frame formulation makes no trial-level prediction from their number: the field presents contents whether one or many inclinations are present.

Incompatibility is what downstream systems resolve using the field's contents, but the field is stated to operate blindly whether or not conflict is present, so incompatibility is no longer a predictor of access (cf. §4).
The reply to commentators accepts that affective contents enter the field but states no valence-dependent access prediction.
Consciousness serves the somatic nervous system: it is a frame that constrains and directs skeletal-muscle output, and conflicts without a skeletomotor plan are stated to lie outside it.
The frame is scoped to skeletal-muscle output; no organism-wide cortical–autonomic coherence variable is proposed.
No dimensionality prediction; the field is described as low-level and unintelligent.
The frame is passive: contents are presented without being evaluated, so metarepresentational precision plays no role.
The theory explicitly declines the implementation level — how neurons produce conscious states is not part of the account — so no cortical signature of access is stated.
No statement relates access to the number of competing action policies.
Policy incompatibility is not a variable in the proposal.
The frame could also underlie emotional feelings and vmPFC heartbeat-evoked responses contribute to preference-based decisions, but no valence-dependent access prediction is stated.
Neural monitoring of cardiac (and gastric) input is the stated generator of first-person perspective, and pre-stimulus heartbeat-evoked responses predict detection.
A cortical response to one visceral signal predicts access, independently of measured bodily state; no organism-wide joint cortical–autonomic metric is specified.
The dimensionality and topology of subjective experience are posed as open questions, without a quantitative prediction.
The frame is a low-level building block not explicitly experienced by itself; no claim about metarepresentational precision.

Pre-stimulus heartbeat-evoked response amplitude in right inferior parietal and ventral anterior cingulate cortex is a stated cortical predictor of detection, framed as a precondition rather than as the signature of access itself.
The transition marker is a learning capacity, not an arbitration load.
No incompatibility term.
Valence is one of the constitutive hallmarks of the UAL profile: learning must be reinforceable by positive and negative evaluation of stimuli.
Embodiment and global accessibility are hallmarks; visceral channels are not separately predicted.
"Global accessibility" and integration across the organism are hallmarks, but not operationalised as a joint cortical-autonomic measurement.
No dimensionality prediction.
No metacognitive-precision prediction.
Deliberately substrate-neutral and comparative; no cortical signature.
The threshold is the appearance of isomorphic neural maps of one body/world, not arbitration load.
No incompatibility term.
Affective consciousness is treated as a distinct and possibly earlier kind than exteroceptive image-based consciousness, with nociceptive/valenced states as its content.
Interoceptive and nociceptive channels are constitutive of affective consciousness in their scheme.
Emphasises unified representation of one body but proposes no organism-wide coherence measure.
No dimensionality prediction.
No metacognitive-precision prediction.
Names neuroanatomical prerequisites (hierarchical maps, reciprocal connectivity) rather than an access signature in humans.
